name: UBT251

lead: UBT251 is an experimental injectable peptide that activates the GLP-1, GIP and glucagon receptors. It is being tested for obesity, type 2 diabetes, kidney disease, sleep apnea and fatty liver disease.
Two 24-week phase 2 trials in China were published in 2026, and phase 3 studies are registered. It is not approved for any use.

paras: As a triple agonist, it is designed to combine appetite and insulin effects of GLP-1 and GIP with the energy-expenditure effects associated with glucagon-receptor activation.
Safety data are limited to early trials. The wider drug class is associated with gastrointestinal side effects. It is available only inside clinical trials.

lead: UBT251 is an investigational long-acting peptide that activates three receptors at once: the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon receptors. It was developed by United Biotechnology, a subsidiary of The United Laboratories International Holdings (TUL) in China, and is given as a once-weekly subcutaneous injection in trials. [1][2]

It is being studied for obesity, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, obstructive sleep apnea and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). In March 2025, TUL announced an exclusive licensing deal with Novo Nordisk covering development and commercialisation outside China. [1][3][4][5][6][7][8]

UBT251 is not an approved medicine in any jurisdiction. Published human evidence comes from a first-in-human phase 1a/1b study and two 24-week phase 2 trials in China, reported in 2026. [2][9][10] It belongs to the same broad class of incretin-based weight-loss peptides that includes semaglutide and tirzepatide, which are discussed in appearance and fat-loss communities, but no community discussion of UBT251 itself is documented here.
infobox: GLP-1 / GIP / glucagon receptor triple agonist (peptide)

paras: UBT251 is a chemically synthesised peptide designed to activate the GLP-1, GIP and glucagon receptors together. [2][1] In the wider class of triple agonists, GLP-1 and GIP signalling are associated with glucose-dependent insulin release and reduced appetite, while glucagon-receptor signalling is associated with increased energy expenditure and effects on liver fat metabolism. [1] Detailed receptor-binding data for UBT251 have not been widely published.

According to Grokipedia, the sponsor applied for clinical-trial approval in China in June 2023 and the US FDA cleared an investigational new drug application in October 2023. [1] Grokipedia also reports that the March 2025 Novo Nordisk agreement included an upfront payment and milestone payments potentially reaching about $2 billion, with TUL retaining rights in China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. [1] These deal figures come from an AI-generated encyclopedia and have not been checked against primary announcements here.

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 1a/1b study described UBT251 as a first-in-human trial examining safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, with a single-ascending-dose part. [2]

In a 24-week multicenter phase 2 trial, 205 adults with overweight or obesity and without type 2 diabetes received once-weekly UBT251 at four dose arms or placebo; the primary endpoint was percentage change in body weight. [9] In a separate 24-week phase 2 trial in 211 Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes, UBT251 arms were compared with 1 mg semaglutide and placebo. Least-squares mean changes in glycated hemoglobin ranged from -2.16% to -1.98% across UBT251 arms, versus -1.77% for semaglutide. [10]

Registered studies include a completed phase 2 obesity study, a recruiting phase 2 study in obesity, studies in chronic kidney disease and MASH, and phase 3 programmes in obesity, type 2 diabetes and obstructive sleep apnea. [3][4][5][6][7][8][11][12][13][14] Grokipedia reports an average weight loss of 15.1% over 12 weeks in phase 1 participants; this figure is not confirmed by the abstracts reviewed. [1]

Detailed adverse-event data from the phase 2 trials were not available in the published abstracts reviewed. Medicines in the GLP-1 receptor agonist class are generally associated with gastrointestinal effects such as nausea and vomiting. The long-term safety profile of UBT251 remains under study.

timeline.event: Clinical-trial application filed in China (June) and US IND cleared (October), per Grokipedia. [1]
Exclusive licensing agreement with Novo Nordisk announced (March); phase 2 studies in obesity and type 2 diabetes begin. [1][11][12]
Phase 1a/1b and phase 2 results published; phase 3 trials registered. [2][9][10][13][14]
